label: GO step late in the episode (trial >= 80) after an unrewarded trial, choosing a2
explanation: Fires only at GO steps (never at D1 or D2) and only in the last part of the episode: zero activity before trial ~55, rate 1.9% at trials 70-79, 6.7% at 80-89, 13% at 90-99. Within that span it needs the previous trial to be unrewarded (95% of mass has prev_reward 0; in_rew -1 penalty trials also fire) and the agent to be choosing a2 (model_act == 2 holds 96% of mass; strong negative choice logit). Co-occurs with low value-head output (value < 7.1 covers all activations), which fits late-episode, unrewarded states. The predicate gets dev precision 0.94, mass recall 0.87, top-quartile coverage 0.99. F1 is only 0.72 because there are many weak activations outside the predicate: late-episode a2 GO steps after a rewarded trial, and trials 70-79. Magnitude grows with episode trial and is largest after no reward. It does not fire on a1 choices (4% of mass), on rewarded-previous-trial GO steps early on, or before trial ~60. Uses only observed or self-computed variables (the agent own GO choice, previous reward, and elapsed trial count), with no future variables.

issues: The factual claims hold. The feature fires only at GO (D1 and D2 have 0 active steps). It is silent before trial 50 (6 steps at 50-59). Rates are 1.9% at trials 70-79, 6.7% at 80-89 and 13.1% at 90-99. 95.7% of mass has model_act==2, a1 has 4.3%, and 94.6% of mass has prev_reward==0. Test scores reproduce: P 0.936, R 0.591, F1 0.725, mass recall 0.86. One small error: 'every activation has value < 7.1' is not exact, since 24 active steps fall in the [7.13, 7.54) value bin.

Systematic omission. The label and explanation do not mention the previous trial's transition, and that is what drives the strongest activations. Inside the predicate, one case stands out: the previous trial was a2, then a RARE transition to S1, then unrewarded, and the agent now repeats a2 (prev_state==1 & prev_action==2). This case has precision 0.995 on 6029 steps (39% of predicted steps). It holds 52% of all activation mass and 69% of the top activation quartile (test: 48% of mass, 64% of the top quartile). The other main case, a2 with a common transition to S2 then unrewarded (prev_state==2, 5754 steps), holds only 16% of mass and 8% of the top quartile. Per step it is about 3x weaker. The profile's prev_common==0 lift (1.7x, 59% of mass) points the same way. So in its strongest form the feature is 'repeat a2 after a rare-unrewarded S1 visit, late in the episode', which is the model-based stay-after-rare-unrewarded case. The label instead treats every unrewarded late a2 GO step the same.

The weak misses are systematic, not scattered. Late a2 GO steps after a REWARDED trial make up 55% of the lowest activation quartile, though only 4.8% of mass. Steps at trials 60-79 after no reward with a2 add 3.7% of mass. The explanation acknowledges both, and they are low-magnitude, so they do not overturn the main predicate.

The value-head correlation does not explain the feature better. (phase==GO)&(value<6.5)&(model_act==2)&(ep_trial>=60) has F1 0.59, and value<7.13 at GO has precision 0.22. The trial-count gating is real and is not just a stand-in for low value.
No future variables are involved. The refinement uses only observed history (prev_state, prev_action, prev_reward) and the agent's own upcoming choice.
skeptic.revised_label: GO step late in the episode (trial >= ~75) after an unrewarded trial, choosing a2. It is strongest when the agent repeats a2 after a2 led by a rare transition to S1 and was unrewarded (stay after rare-unrewarded). It is weaker after an unrewarded common a2 trial to S2, and weak or absent after rewarded trials.
